channel.title: Hacker News - English
channel.description: Hacker News articles summarized and translated to English

item.title: Show HN: Getting GLM 5.2 running on my slow computer
item.description:
📝 Tiny engine, immense model. Quantization kernels: int8 / packed int4 / packed int2, per-row scales, AVX2, dequant-on-use. Download the model A pre-converted GLM-5.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri

item.title: A road to Lisp: Why Lisp
item.description:
📝 Because in Lisp you can do things that are not possible in other languages. Extensibility Lisp is extensible within itself. Not only will you write code for your programs, but you can write code that extends Lisp itself.
🔗 Read more: https://scotto.me/blog/2026-07-09-why-lisp/

item.title: Interview with Mitchell Hashimoto about Ghostty and Zig
item.description:
📝 I also really wanted to play with Zig. What do you think about non-legacy terminal APIs. Main screen is like your shell with scrollback etc.
🔗 Read more: https://alexalejandre.com/programming/interview-with-mitchell-hashimoto/

item.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
item.description:
📝 pgrust A Postgres rewrite in Rust. pgrust is disk compatible with Postgres and can boot from an existing Postgres 18. Background: Original pgrust launch: https://malisper.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/malisper/pgrust

item.title: How GitHub gave every repository a durable owner
item.description:
📝 Michael Recachinas is a Staff Security Engineer at GitHub, where he leads large-scale security programs focused on vulnerability management, secure development lifecycle tooling, and developer-first security automation. He has spent his career building systems that operate at scale and help teams make the secure choice the easy choice.
🔗 Read more: https://github.blog/security/application-security/how-github-gave-every-repository-a-durable-owner/

item.title: AI content is everywhere on social media, especially LinkedIn
item.description:
📝 On four out of five platforms, longer content was more likely to be AI-generated than shortform content. 72% of items over 250 words) were fully AI-generated. 35x more likely to be AI-generated than a comment.
🔗 Read more: https://www.pangram.com/blog/ai-in-your-feed

item.title: Show HN: I built a web tool to see and edit what an AI thinks before it answers
item.description:
📝 Lucid watches a language model think. Watch which concepts enter the workspace, at which layer, and which ones the model holds but never says. The lens is fit once per model.
🔗 Read more: https://lucid.earthpilot.ai
